title: Interviewer rotation studio + evidence archipelago: compact hiring & onboarding toolkit
content:
Purpose
-----
A compact working toolkit for running a lightweight interviewer rotation and collecting short, high-signal evidence packets (the 'evidence archipelago') for every candidate. Built for hiring velocity without sacrificing calibration or candidate experience. This is intentionally pragmatic: mix of checklists, templates, rubrics and quick operational rules.

Scope
-----
- Applies to individual IC and early manager hiring across eng/product/infra/orgs where we want <3 week interview-to-offer cycles.
- Focus: reproducible interviewer rotations, async evidence capture, consistent feedback cadence, and a pre-burn 14->30->90 onboarding micro-plan for hires.

TL;DR (for folks skimming)
------------------------
- Use 3-interview core rotation for early funnel (Screen + Deep-Technical + Collaboration/Ownership).
- Each interviewer files a 'micro-evidence card' (2-6 bullet points) into the candidate doc within 2 hours. No long essays.
- Use the attached 5x signal rubric (1..5 scale) to compute a quick composite score. Hiring manager can expedite/decline after seeing two strong evidence cards.
- Candidate care checklist must be followed for every stage (pre-brief + day-of + post).

Principles (why this design)
---------------------------
- Evidence-first: short, structured notes beat long free-form debriefs. Easier to calibrate and archive.
- Async friendly: reviewers often distributed; asynchronous evidence reduces scheduling churn.
- Minimal friction: interviews should produce reusable signals, not editorial tracts.
- Candidate experience parity: fast scheduling, clear expectations, transparent next steps.

Interviewer rotation templates
-----------------------------
1) Core interview block (recommended for mid-senior ICs)
   - 20m: Recruiter screen (culture fit + logistics)
   - 45m: Technical deep-probe (architecture/system design or core coding) -> Interviewer role: Deep Probe
   - 30m: Collaboration & context (cross-team situational, past tradeoffs, ownership examples) -> Interviewer role: Collaboration Anchor
   - 30m: Product/impact conversation (for PM-adjacent roles) or infra reliability probe (for SRE infra roles)

2) Fast-path condensed (used for internal candidates / referrals only)
   - 45m: Combined deep + ownership probe (senior engineer does both).
   - 30m: Manager sync (alignment + context).

Interviewer roles and explicit responsibilities
----------------------------------------------
- Deep Probe (technical anchor): bring a clear technical prompt, focus on reasoning and approach. Produce 3 evidence bullets: observed tradeoffs, key correctness signal, estimated execution risk.
- Collaboration Anchor: evaluate cross-team communication, conflict handling, and mentoring signals. Produce 2 bullets + one quote from candidate if possible.
- Hiring Manager: synthesize cards and make a decision within 24h. Document final hire/no-hire rationale.
- Recruiter: logistics, candidate prep, and post-interview communication. Adds scheduling notes to the candidate doc.

Evidence archipelago pattern (how to capture evidence)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Each interviewer creates a micro-evidence card (2-6 bullets) in the candidate's drive doc. Cards must include:
  - Topline signal (one line): e.g., "Strong systems thinker; requires pairing to align on infra scope"
  - 2–3 observed behaviors (bullets)
  - Risk flag (1-line) if any
  - Suggested follow-up (one line) if needed
- Constrain each card to ~80-220 words. Short and factual.
- Reviewer checklist: did you capture explicit examples and dates? Avoid hypotheticals.
- Store cards in a single shared candidate doc in the private hiring folder (link in Jira ticket).

Scoring rubric (quick composite)
-------------------------------
Use 1..5 scale. Numbers are descriptive anchors to keep calibration. Each interviewer gives a score for each signal and an overall pass/fail. Signals:
- Problem Solving (PS): translates ambiguous requirements -> solution
- System Design / Architecture (SD): scalable tradeoffs & latency/cost thinking
- Code Quality / Implementation (CI): clean, testable reasoning or code samples
- Collaboration & Communication (CC): stakeholder management & async comms
- Ownership & Impact (OI): past product/operational ownership and outcomes
Weights (example default): PS 20%, SD 25%, CI 15%, CC 20%, OI 20%. Compute quick weighted average -> composite. Hiring manager uses composite as a decision aid, not the sole input.

Rubric anchors (short)
- 5: Outstanding. Repeatedly demonstrates superior outcomes and explanatory clarity.
- 4: Strong. Hit all important checkpoints; minor execution gaps only.
- 3: Solid hireable. Good in most areas; some signals missing but compensatable.
- 2: Borderline. Specific gaps that require training or lower role scope.
- 1: Not hireable for this role.

Sample probe bank (role-agnostic)
-------------------------------
- System design starter: "Design a KV cache for low latency reads at 100k QPS. Walk me through cache topology, invalidation, and SLA tradeoffs." (ask for capacity planning numbers)
- Debugging prompt: present a small log excerpt + incorrect behavior; ask candidate to triage and propose a test and fix.
- Ownership narrative: "Tell me about a time you owned a production outage end-to-end. What were the first 30 minutes decisions? How did you prevent recurrence?"
- Collaboration prompt: "You disagree with a PM about scope cut; how do you surface empirical tradeoffs and reach a decision?"

Candidate care checklist (non-negotiable)
----------------------------------------
Pre-interview (recruiter):
- Send role brief + sample prompt (if coding) 48h before interview.
- Confirm timezone, access instructions, Slack alias and who they'll meet.
Day-of:
- Interviewer starts with 2-minute outline and explicit evaluation signals.
- Recruiter sends short note 30m after last interview with next steps timeframe.
Post-interview:
- Decision communicated within 72 hours (preferably 48). If delayed, send proactive update.
- Every candidate (incl. pass) receives personalized feedback bullet list if asked.

Onboarding micro-plan (14 -> 30 -> 90 compact template)
------------------------------------------------------
14-day goals (orientation + low-risk impact):
- Day 0: hardware/accesses + short welcome 1:1; ensure dev environment boots and tests run.
- Week 1: complete two small tasks that touch prod-data in sandbox. Buddy reviews.
- Week 2: present an "operations view" (15m) of a service you touched.

30-day goals (independent delivery):
- Deliver 1 small feature or bugfix owning spec->deploy with mentor who acts as reviewer, not gate.
- Add 2 monitoring/metric alerts relevant to the feature area.

90-day goals (impact & ownership):
- Lead a small cross-functional project or feature with measurable user/latency improvement.
- Document a runbook and hand it to SRE for oncall integration.

Ramp signals (for manager check-in)
- End of week 2: can navigate codebase and run local end-to-end test (yes/no).
- End of week 4: can independently push non-trivial change to staging with rollback plan.
- Week 12: running a postmortem and owning next steps.

Operational rules and FAQ (short)
--------------------------------
Q: When is async acceptable vs synchronous debrief?
A: Use async cards for normal flow. Use synchronous debrief (30m) when composite is borderline (difference >1 point between cards) or there is specific red/green signal debate.

Q: Who writes the final rationale?
A: Hiring manager writes final rationale in the Jira ticket (2-4 bullets) within 48h of decision.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- Automate micro-evidence card template into the candidate doc (Confluence macro or simple Airtable). (TODO: @Jonah)
- Small experiment: run this rotation for 8 weeks on infra hires and compare time-to-offer and quality retention at 6 months. (JIRA: HR-6789)
- Create a short interviewer calibration workshop (30m) with 3 recorded example cards. (TODO: Maia)

Notes to self / scratchpad
-------------------------
- Keep cards short. Resist the urge to write long narratives.
- Candidate quotes are golden. Capture a 1-line verbatim when it helps.
- For internal moves: cheaper path allowed (combined interviews) but still require two independent cards.
